sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854

items.q: Sustained sympathetic activity in pheochromocytoma leads to:
opts: ↑ intravascular volume, DM and weight loss
items.exp: Leads to ↑ intravascular volume (with ↓GFR → hypercalcaemia → acute abdominal pain, and postural hypotension), DM and weight loss. (Book p854)

items.q: Pheochromocytoma causes 2° paraneoplastic polycythaemia by producing:
items.exp: Pheochromocytoma produces erythropoietin (EPO) → 2° paraneoplastic polycythemia. (Book p854)

items.q: The m/c symptom of the classic triad — episodic headache — occurs in:
items.exp: Triad: episodic headache (95%, m/c symptom), palpitation/tachycardia, profuse sweating. (Book p854)

items.q: The other two corners of the symptom triad are:
items.exp: Palpitation/tachycardia and profuse sweating complete the triad. (Book p854)

items.q: Pallor during spells in pheochromocytoma should raise suspicion of:
items.exp: Pallor: suspect malignancy. Other features: abdominal pain, palpitation (sinus tachy), perspiration, panic attack (75%), postural hypotension, weight loss, hyperadrenergic spells. (Book p854)

items.q: The m/c SIGN — episodic hypertension — is seen in:
items.exp: Episodic hypertension (75–85%) is the m/c sign; sustained only in 20%, giving resistant young hypertension. (Book p854)
Sustained only in 20% — resistant young hypertension. (Book p854)

items.q: Normal BP between spells is found in:
Match postural hypotension criteria (any one) — 1) Heart rate  2) Systolic BP  3) Diastolic BP … A) ↓ >20 mmHg  B) ↑ >30/min  C) ↓ >10 mmHg
items.exp: Supine then standing (2–5 min): ↑HR >30/min, ↓systolic >20 mmHg or ↓diastolic >10 mmHg = postural hypotension (75%). (Book p854)
